headline: Granted a permit for a car wash, gas station, and convenience store at 1187 Union Street; recommended removing downtown floor area ratio limits.
summary: Staff said the Fire Department had no concerns about taller downtown buildings, and there is no current demand for skyscrapers. The Union Street permit requires state approval of a traffic permit and a fix to the stormwater narrative. Other items covered the coming election of officers and commuter traffic.
decisions: Approved the minutes of the October 6, 2026 meeting, with all voting members in favor.
Adopted the findings and decisions for 511 Maine Ave and 6 Bangor Mall Blvd, with all voting members in favor.
Recommended that the amendment removing Floor Area Ratio from the Downtown Development District pass, with all voting members in favor.
Found the 1187 Union Street application complete and all fees paid, with all voting members in favor.
Found that the Union Street project meets the traffic rules, with the condition that the state approves its Traffic Movement Permit, with all voting members in favor.
Granted the Land Development Permit for the car wash, gas station, and convenience store at 1187 Union Street, with conditions, with all voting members in favor.

PLANNING BOARD

COUNCIL CHAMBERS, 1ST FLOOR OF CITY HALL 
73 HARLOW STREET 
 
MEETING MINUTES 
 
  Board Members Present:  Chair Jonathan Boucher 
Vice Chair Janet Jonas  
Ted Brush 
Trisha Hayes 
Ken Huhn 
Greg Hobson 
Ross Whitford 
 
      
City Staff Present:   Anja Collette, Planning Officer  
        Matt Altiero, Planning Analyst 
Grace Innis, Assistant City Solicitor 
Jefferson Davis, Engineering Director 
 
 
Chair Boucher called the meeting to order at 7:00 P.M.  
 
OLD BUSINESS 
1. Meeting Minutes – October 6, 2026 
Member Huhn moved to approve the minutes of October 6, 2026. Seconded by Member Hobson. Roll call vote 
conducted – all voting members in favor, none opposed. Motion passed. 
2. Adopt Findings & Decisions for 511 Maine Ave and 6 Bangor Mall Blvd 
Member Brush moved to adopt the findings and decisions for 511 Maine Ave and 6 Bangor Mall Blvd. 
Seconded by Vice Chair Jonas. Roll call vote conducted – all voting members in favor, none opposed. Motion 
passed. 
NEW BUSINESS 
1. Amending the Land Development Code, § 165, Attachment 2 -  Schedule A, Urban 
Developed Area to Remove Floor Area Ratio (FAR) from the Downtown 
Development District (DDD) 
 
Chair Boucher introduced the agenda item.
Page  2 | 7 
 
City of Bangor Planning Division 
Planning Board Meeting Minutes – Tuesday, October 20, 2026 
Planning Officer Collette provided an overview of the proposal to eliminate the Floor Area Ratio (FAR) 
limit from the Downtown Development District (DDD) due to it being an outdated standard. She shared 
that after receiving feedback, staff discussed whether height limits are needed downtown with the Fire 
Department and Bangor International Airport. The Fire Department did not express concerns with taller 
buildings and staff would run anything like a skyscraper by the airport fir st; Collette noted though that 
there is not a demand for skyscrapers in the City at this time.  
 
Chair Boucher asked for any questions from the Board – there were one.   
 
Chair Boucher opened public comment – there were none. Public comment closed. 
 
Member Huhn moved that the Board recommend that the amendment to the Land Development Code, 
§ 165, Attachment 2 - Schedule A, Urban Developed Area to Remove Floor Area Ratio (FAR) from the 
Downtown Development District (DDD)  ought to pass. Seconded by Vice Chair  Jonas. Roll call vote 
conducted – all voting members in favor, none opposed. Motion passed. 
 
2. Land Development Permit Application – Major Site Development and Conditional 
Use – 1187 Union Street – Map-Lots R24-001-A, R24-001-B, R24-001-C – RH Foster 
Energy, LLC – Land Development Permit Application – Major Site Development and 
Conditional Use for proposed car wash, gas station, and convenience store at property 
located at 1187 Union Street, Map-Lots R24-001-A, R24-001-B, and R24-001-C, in the 
Shopping and Personal Service District (S&PS). Applicant/Owner: RH Foster Energy, 
LLC. 
Chair Boucher introduced the agenda item. 
 
Vice Chair Jonas moved that the Board finds the application was deemed complete on October 20th, 
2026, all applicable fees for the project have been paid, and the proposed project is a Major Site 
Development and Conditional Use. Seconded by Member Hobson. Roll call vote conducted – all voting 
members in favor, none opposed. Motion passed. 
 
Applicant Representative Sean Thies presented on the project, walking through the site plan and 
associated proposals. 
 
Planning Officer Collette noted to include stormwater permitting in the final decision.  
 
Member Huhn asked whether there is not natural gas located at the site or if propane is better. Applicant 
Representative Thies responded that since the applicant sells propane, they typically use propane tanks 
to serve their stores.  
 
Member Brush asked whether the applicant anticipates a change in the traffic pattern – Applicant 
Representative Thies responded that the applicant is doing a Traffic Movement Permit with Maine 
Department of Transportation based. Thies added that the increased store size and proposed changes 
does generates more trips, and a majority of the trips are pass by, meaning vehicles that are already on 
the road.
Page  3 | 7 
 
City of Bangor Planning Division 
Planning Board Meeting Minutes – Tuesday, October 20, 2026 
Vice Chair Jonas asked about the increasing amount of traffic in the afternoon and in commuting hours, 
as well as the traffic anticipated to go through the intersection in any direction. She expressed that there 
may be opportunities based on the traffic study to work on the traffic pattern, specifically going west on 
Griffin Road into the intersection. Jonas noted that as it is the closest gas station to the airport, it likely 
receives additional traffic in the summer.  
 
Vice Chair Jonas discussed the proposed reuse of existing buffers, expressing that most of the existing 
trees appear unwell. She asked whether they are intended to be replaced and whether the City can 
require that. Applicant Representative Thies responded that a lot of them are being replaced and referred 
to the landscape plan to describe which are intended for replacement.  
 
Vice Chair Jonas expressed appreciation for explaining the catchment and how the stormwater ru noff 
was determined. She noted that there was a mistype with a reference to the incorrect location that needs 
to be corrected.  
 
Engineering Director Davis shared that he had a scope meeting with the Department of Transportation 
and that the way the site is proposed vastly improves site circulation. He noted that the plan pulls existing 
access away from the intersection of Griffin Road and Union Street and removes the exit closest to Griffin 
Road and Union Street. Davis discussed restriping Union Street and creating a teardrop island north of 
the intersection coming inbound. He expressed he does not have concerns about the project. 
 
Planning Officer Collette noted that the Board can condition the approval that the incorrect location in the 
stormwater narrative is corrected.  
 
Chair Boucher asked for elaboration on going from seven curb cuts to four. Applicant Representative 
Thies responded that there is currently four on Union Street and three on Griffin Road, and the project is 
replacing all of those with the one full movement on Union Street. Thies added that now that the car wash 
and convenience store are connected, vehicles can go directly back and forth instead of onto Griffin 
Road.  
 
Chair Boucher asked for questions or comments from staff – there were none. 
 
Chair Boucher opened public comment – there were none. Public comment closed. 
 
Chair Boucher asked the board for any questions or comments – there were none. 
 
Member Huhn moved that the Board finds that, based on Exhibits 2 and 14, the applicant satisfied §165-
33.1 of the Land Development Code regarding best management practices of Erosion and Sediment 
Control. Seconded by Member Brush.  Roll call vote conducted – all voting members in favor, none 
opposed. Motion passed. 
 
Member Hobson moved that the Board finds, that based on Exhibit 2 and 33, the applicant satisfied §165-
62 of the Land Development Code regarding providing adequate visual clearance on corner lots, §165-
64’s requirements for side yard width, §165- 65’s requirements for yard space for  group buildings, and 
§165-68’s requirements of minimum lot frontage. Seconded by Vice Chair Jonas. Roll call vote conducted 
– all voting members in favor, none opposed. Motion passed.
Page  4 | 7 
 
City of Bangor Planning Division 
Planning Board Meeting Minutes – Tuesday, October 20, 2026 
Vice Chair Jonas moved that t he Board finds that, based on Exhibit 2 and 33, the applicant satisfied 
§165-72 of the Land Development Code regarding the required number of parking spaces, §165 -73’s 
requirements regarding parking area location and screening, and §165 -74’s requirements regarding 
parking area design, construction and maintenance. Seconded by Member Brush. Roll call vote 
conducted – all voting members in favor, none opposed. Motion passed. 
 
Member Brush moved that the Board finds that, based on Exhibit 2 and 33, the applicant satisfied §165-
76 of the Land Developm ent Code regarding the required number of loading spaces, §165- 77’s 
requirements regarding loading space sizes, and §165- 78’s general requirements for loading spaces.  
Seconded by Member Hobson. Roll call vote conducted –  all voting members in favor, none opposed. 
Motion passed. 
 
Member Hayes moved that the Board finds that, based on Exhibits 2, 19, and 30, the applicant satisfied 
§165-79 of the Land Development Code regarding providing the necessary utility services required, §165-
80’s requirements regarding providing adequate water and sewerage services, and 165- 83’s 
requirements regarding providing adequate electrical service. Seconded by Member Brush. Roll call vote 
conducted – all voting members in favor, none opposed. Motion passed. 
 
Member Huhn moved that the Board finds that, based on Exhibits 2 and 13, the applicant satisfied §165-
81 of the Land Development Code regarding providing adequate lighting and preventing light pollution 
and trespass. Seconded my Member Brush. Roll call vote conducted – all voting members in favor, none 
opposed. Motion passed. 
 
Member Brush moved that the Board finds that, based on Exhibits 2 and 31, the applicant satisfied §165-
82’s requirements regarding having adequate fire protection. Seconded by Member Huhn. Roll call vote 
conducted – all voting members in favor, none opposed. Motion passed. 
 
Member Hobson The Board finds that, based on Exhibits 2, 30, and 32, the applicant satisfied §165- 84 
of the Land Development Code regarding providing adequate storm drainage and storm water offset. 
Seconded by Vice Chair Jonas. Roll call vote conducted –  all voting members in favor, none opposed. 
Motion passed. 
 
Vice Chair Jonas moved that t he Board finds that, based on Exhibits 2 and 30, the applicant satisfied 
§165-85 and §165-86 of the Land Development Code regarding providing information on sanitary flows 
and compliance with sewer regulations.  Seconded by Member Hobson. Roll call vote conducted – all 
voting members in favor, none opposed. Motion passed. 
 
Member Huhn moved that t he Board finds that, based on Exhibits 2, 21, 22, 25 -26, 30, and 33, the 
applicant satisfied § 165- 135 of the Land Development Code regarding height limit, floor area ratio, 
impervious surface ratio, and buffer yards.  Seconded by Member Brush. Roll call vote conducted – all 
voting members in favor, none opposed. Motion passed. 
 
Member Hobson moved that t he Board finds that, based on the findings made in Parts 1 and 2 of this 
document, the Project meets the requirements of §165-101B for uses within the Shopping and Personal 
Service District (S&PS). Seconded by Vice Chair Jonas. Roll call vote conducted –  all voting members 
in favor, none opposed. Motion passed.
Page  5 | 7 
 
City of Bangor Planning Division 
Planning Board Meeting Minutes – Tuesday, October 20, 2026 
Vice Chair Jonas moved that the Board finds that, provided the Project is found to meet the requirements 
of §165-9 in Part 5 below, and based on Exhibits 2 and 34, the Project meets the requirements of §165-
101D for the conditional uses of retail auto service, drive-in business, and gasoline service station within 
the Shopping and Personal Service District  (S&PS). Seconded by Member Hobson. Roll call vote 
conducted – all voting members in favor, none opposed. Motion passed. 
 
Member Hayes moved that the Board finds that, based on Exhibits 2, 8, 28, and 30, the applicant satisfied 
Land Development Code §165 -114B’s requirement that the proposed parking and loading layout are 
arranged in a reasonable and safe configuration, including the provision for safe pedestrian travel to all 
on-site uses, and §165- 114C’s requirement that all proposed access drives are reas onably necessary 
and safe. Seconded by Member Whitford. Roll call vote conducted – all voting members in favor, none 
opposed. Motion passed. 
 
Member Brush moved that t he Board finds that, based on Exhibits 2, 9, 10, 15, 16, 30, and 32, the 
applicant satisfied Land Development Code §165- 114D’s requirement that the proposed development 
will not have unreasonable adverse effects on abutting or downstream properties or protected resources 
such as wetlands, lakes, streams or brooks, and that all downstream channels or municipal stormwater 
collection systems have adequate capacity to carry the flow without significant negative effects.  
Seconded by Member Hayes. Roll call vote conducted – all voting members in favor, none opposed. 
Motion passed. 
 
Member Huhn moved that the Board finds that, based on Exhibits 2 and 13, the applicant satisfied Land 
Development Code §165-114E’s requirements that all outdoor lighting shall be designed, installed and 
maintained to avoid unreasonable adverse effects from light pollution.  Seconded by Member Hobson. 
Roll call vote conducted – all voting members in favor, none opposed. Motion passed. 
 
Member Brush moved that the Board finds that, based on Exhibits 2 and 8, the applicant satisfied Land 
Development Code §165- 114F’s requirements for landscaping. Seconded by Member Huhn. Roll call 
vote conducted – all voting members in favor, none opposed. Motion passed. 
 
Member Huhn moved that the Board finds that, based on Exhibits 2 and 30, the applicant satisfied Land 
Development Code §165-114G, requiring buildings to be situated to avoid unreasonable adverse effects 
on adjacent properties or public rights-of-way. Seconded by Member Hobson. Roll call vote conducted – 
all voting members in favor, none opposed. Motion passed. 
 
Member Hayes moved that t he Board finds that, based on Exhibits 2, 4, 9- 11, and 32, the applicant 
satisfied Land Development Code §165-114K, requiring that site developments needing approval under 
38 M.R.S.A. §420-D, meet the standards of 38. M.R.S.A. §420-D(1), as amended, and the requirements 
of Department of Environmental Protection regulations, Chapters 500, 501. and 502. Seconded by Vice 
Chair Jonas. Roll call vote conducted – all voting members in favor, none opposed. Motion passed. 
 
Vice Chair Jonas moved that the Board finds that, based on the findings made in Parts 1-4 of Section IV 
of this document, the applicant satisfied Land Development Code §165 -9A(1)’s requirements regarding 
not requiring a variance of development or other standards. Seconded by Member Hobson. Roll call vote 
conducted – all voting members in favor, none opposed. Motion passed.
Page  6 | 7 
 
City of Bangor Planning Division 
Planning Board Meeting Minutes – Tuesday, October 20, 2026 
Member Hobson moved that the Board finds that, based on Exhibits 2,18, and 30, the applicant satisfied 
Land Development Code §165- 9A(2)’s requirements regarding not creating unreasonable traffic 
congestion or hazardous conditions on contiguous or adjacent streets, with the condition that the 
applicant’s Traffic Movement Permit application is approved by the Maine Department of Transportation. 
Seconded by Member Brush. Roll call vote conducted –  all voting members in favor, none opposed. 
Motion passed. 
 
Member Huhn moved that the Board finds that, based on the findings made in Parts 1-4 of Section IV of 
this document, the applicant satisfied Land Development Code §165-9A(3)’s requirements for providing 
and maintaining adequate and appropriate utilities, fire protection, drainage, parking and loading and 
other necessary site improvements. Seconded by Vice Chair Jonas. Roll call vote conducted – all voting 
members in favor, none opposed. Motion passed. 
 
Vice Chair Jonas moved that t he Board finds that, based on Exhibits 2, 8, and 24- 26, the applicant 
satisfied Land Development Code §165- 9A(4)’s requirements regarding the proposed use being 
appropriate for the location in which it is sought because it conforms to the general physical development 
pattern of the immediate area. Seconded by Member Brush. Roll call vote conducted – all voting members 
in favor, none opposed. Motion passed. 
 
Vice Chair Jonas moved that t he Board finds that the project meets the requirements for a Land 
Development Permit and Stormwater Permit  for a Major Site Development and Conditional Use and 
therefore, the Board grants the Land Development Permit for the proposed project with the conditions: 
that the applicant must receive approval for their Traffic Movement Permit application from the Maine 
Department of Transportation, and the Stormwater Narrative is corrected to reflect that the parcels are 
located in the City of Bangor. Seconded by Member Hobson. Roll call vote conducted – all voting 
members in favor, none opposed. Motion passed. 
 
 
OTHER BUSINESS 
 
 
1. Reminder about election of officers in the new year 
 
Chair Boucher reminded the Board that they are not to be meeting on Election Day, November 3 rd. He 
noted the next meeting will be November 17th.  
 
Chair Boucher discussed the election of officers in the new year. Planning Officer Collette recommended 
the Board think about who they would like to nominate for Chair and Vice Chair, and noted they can 
nominate themselves.  
 
Chair Boucher provided an overview of being Chair, describing that he will receive an overview of what’s 
coming from Planning Officer Collette in advance and have the opportunity to ask clarifying questions. 
He discussed using a template to build out an agenda to include each detail required within the bulleted 
sections, as well as using template language. Boucher described the responsibility of reading the packet, 
conducting roll call votes, and provide reminders throughout. He not ed that while he is happy to serve 
again if there is no interest, he wanted to open up the opportunity.
Page  7 | 7 
 
City of Bangor Planning Division 
Planning Board Meeting Minutes – Tuesday, October 20, 2026 
Vice Chair Jonas discussed coordinating with Chair Boucher in the instance where he would be unable 
to attend.  
 
Member Hobson commended Chair Boucher for doing a great job as chair.   
 
 
2. Follow-Up/Thoughts on Land Use Plan Updates 
 
Planning Officer Collette provided an update that staff is approximately halfway through the new articles with 
the consultants and are coordinating with the airport to create an overlay district. She discussed integrating 
state laws into the new code, but with the current timeline, they may need to proceed with integrating the state 
laws into the current code in the spring.  
 
Planning Officer Collette discussed the upcoming Growth Boundary Workshop on Thursday, October 29th at 
6:00 PM, where staff will provide an explanation of the process, answer questions, and receive feedback.  
 
Vice Chair Jonas discussed increased traffic and asked about the possibility to create commuter lots on the 
outskirts of Bangor to alleviate traffic. Planning Officer Collette clarified if Vice Chair Jonas is referring to a park 
and ride. Collette expressed that that she believes a contributing factor is that there is not enough affordable 
housing within the city causing people that work in the city to have to commute in. She shared that the housing 
study found that 80% of people who work in city limits live outside of the city, and that is tied to lack of 
affordable housing. Collette noted that while zoning is one piece of it (with the hope being that creating more 
allowances for density and affordable housing will help with the shortage), but there are many other factors 
affecting housing availability. 
 
Engineering Director Davis discussed that the historic traffic numbers have not changed much since 2000, but 
that pockets of the area affected may change. He noted Broadway is a corridor that needs to be looked at and 
is impacted by commuters. Vice Chair Jonas added that Route 2 may need attention as well.  
 
Meeting adjourned at 7:57 PM. 
 
Respectfully submitted, 
 
Kayleigh Rienas 
Development Assistant 
Planning Division
